summary: RFC 7865 and RFC 7866 disagree about how SIPREC recording metadata should be labeled, and neither registered the new media type. This RFC corrects that and registers the media type.

plainLanguage.summary: Two instruction sheets gave different names to the same thing. This fixes the mix-up and registers one official name.

questions: which siprec media type is correct
subtitle: Fixes a media type name conflict between two SIPREC RFCs and registers the type with IANA.

tldr.problem: RFC 7865 and RFC 7866 contradict each other on how recording metadata is labeled, and neither registered the media type with IANA.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7866 is updated so every instance of application/rs-metadata becomes application/rs-metadata+xml, and the media type is registered.
tldr.outcome: SIPREC now uses one name, application/rs-metadata+xml, and the type is registered; this resolves an erratum against RFC 7866.

today: RFC 9806 is a Proposed Standard published in June 2025. It updates RFC 7866 and has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: The Naming Conflict
sections.content:
The SIP-based Media Recording (SIPREC) protocol is defined by RFC 7865 and RFC 7866. The former specifies application/rs-metadata+xml to identify metadata content, while the latter uses application/rs-metadata.

Since RFC 7865 defines SIPREC metadata, it was treated as normative, and an erratum was filed against RFC 7866. This document resolves it. Neither document registered the media type with IANA, and this one does.
sections.plainLanguage: One sheet said one name and the other said a slightly different one. The first sheet's name wins.

sections.title: The Update to RFC 7866
sections.content:
Each instance of application/rs-metadata in RFC 7866 is replaced with application/rs-metadata+xml. That is the whole change to the older text.

The updates clarify inconsistencies in published documents and introduce no new security considerations beyond those in RFC 7866.
sections.plainLanguage: Everywhere the short name appears, write the longer name instead.

sections.title: Media Type Registration
sections.content:
The registration gives type name application and subtype name rs-metadata+xml, with no required or optional parameters. Encoding considerations are the same as for application/xml in RFC 7303. The published specifications are RFC 7865 and RFC 9806.

It is used by Session Recording Clients (SRCs) and Session Recording Servers (SRSs). Intended usage is COMMON, with no restrictions on where it can be used. The contact is the IETF SIPCORE Working Group and the change controller is the IETF.
sections.plainLanguage: The name is now written in the official list, with who uses it and who looks after it.
